user: I'm CUS-0004. Transaction TX-0401, 240.00 EUR: the goods never arrived. Which reason code applies?
answer:
The reason code that matches your situation is **goods_not_received**. Use it when you paid for goods and they were never delivered.

Under our dispute rules, this code has a 90-day window counted from the transaction date. A dispute filed after the window closes is not eligible. The code also has to match what happened, because a dispute filed under the wrong code is declined and would have to be refiled, which could push it past the window.

I haven't checked TX-0401 yet, so I can't confirm it is within the window. I can run an eligibility check on it now. If it is eligible, I can then open the dispute, but I'll only do that with your confirmation.

fragments.text:
Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each dispute reason code has its own window, counted in days from the
transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Reason code guide
## Choosing a code
The reason code must match what actually happened. A dispute filed under the
wrong code is declined and must be refiled, which may push it past its window.

Payment dispute rules
## Eligibility conditions
A dispute is eligible only if all of the following hold: the reason code is
valid; the transaction status is settled; the transaction date is within the
reason code's window relative to the current date; and no customer-level
restriction applies (for example, an account under compliance review cannot
open new disputes until the review concludes).

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.
